5-HTP.about: Serotonin precursor: ~65% remission, but old RCTs, no placebo; monotherapy is not recommended.
5-HTP.caution: 5-hydroxytryptophan (serotonin precursor). A Cochrane review shows that older RCTs (1960s-80s) had methodological problems. Current data is limited. For depression: not recommended as monotherapy. Caution: serotonin syndrome in combination with SSRI/MAOI. Side effects: nausea, GI disorders. Quality of supplements varies (contamination with eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome in the past).
5-HTP.food_sources: There is no food with 5-HTP - it is a metabolite of tryptophan; tryptophan itself is in meat/milk, but the path is different.
5-HTP.guidelines: Cochrane 2001: 2 RCT (n=64), OR 4.10 - low quality. MA 2020: remission 0.65, g 1.11, almost no placebo.
5-HTP.how_to_choose: Only with a doctor; standardized product, 100-300 mg; not with SSRI/MAOI; risk of nausea and contamination (EMS).
mechs: Mood/sleep in short courses; NOT with SSRI
Correction of serotonergic dysfunction in depression
Remission 65% (0.55–0.78), H^ 1.11; RCT quality is low
Limitations: few high-quality RCTs, no placebo, heterogeneity
5-HTP.myths: "Nature's Antidepressant" - RCT 1960-80s, no placebo. “Safe with SSRI” - serotonin syndrome. “Remission 65%” - I² 76%.
5-HTP.name: 5-HTP
5-HTP.onset: The effect is not systematized: some of the schemes last for weeks; there is little data on speed and stability.
5-HTP.title: 5-HTP
5-HTP.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
5-HTP.who_needs: The issue of depression is decided by the doctor; self-administration is not indicated - RCT quality is low, risk of serotonin syndrome with SSRI/MAOI.

Alpha-GPC.about: Acetylcholine precursor: for dementia - weak plus; in healthy people, 315-630 mg improves Stroop after an hour.
Alpha-GPC.caution: Alpha-GPC (L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine) is a precursor of acetylcholine. There are NO meta-analyses or systematic reviews in the database. There may be data in individual RCTs, but no systematic evaluation. Its popularity in sports nutrition is not supported by evidence.
effects: Memory (only in combination with donepezil in patients)
Alpha-GPC.food_sources: Purified phospholipid, not a product; Choline is found in eggs and liver, but not in the A-GPC form.
Alpha-GPC.guidelines: MA 2023 (PMID 36683513, 7 RCT): with donepezil cognition MD 1.72; solo vs placebo MD 3.50; There is no sports facility.
Alpha-GPC.how_to_choose: Standard 300-600 mg/day in courses; for dementia - adjunct with a doctor; A healthy person can’t wait for a “memory boost.”
mechs: Sports power and cognition in the elderly (weak)
Acetylcholine precursor in combination with donepezil
ADAS-Cog 12 weeks: −13.9% vs −0.9%; in combination with donepezil (119)
Acute cognitive boost in healthy people after a single dose
Stroop faster (d=0.61) after 60 min; N-Back/Flanker no difference (n=20)
Cognition with slight decrease due to T2D (1200 mg/d)
MMSE difference +1.7 is significant at 12 months; 6 months - no effect (n=36)
Alpha-GPC.myths: “Improves memory for everyone” - memory/fluency is not visible in MA. “Treats dementia itself” - effect with donepezil. “Boost for athletes” - only Stroop, n=20.
Alpha-GPC.name: Alpha-GPC
Alpha-GPC.onset: Healthy Stroop faster after 60 min (without N-Back); if it decreases, weeks of therapy.
Alpha-GPC.title: Alpha-GPC
Alpha-GPC.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
Alpha-GPC.who_needs: Elderly with dementia - adjunct to therapy (by doctor); with T2D with a decrease - a weak signal; healthy - spot Stroop (n=20).

B. lactis.about: Bifidobacterium lactis: the only probiotic with a significant effect on stool frequency in chronic constipation; in other settings, data are limited.
B. lactis.caution: The studies have high heterogeneity and risk of bias, so interpretation of the results requires caution.
B. lactis.course: A course as part of the treatment of chronic constipation or functional abdominal discomfort.
B. lactis.dosage: The exact dose is not given in the abstracts; In some studies, B. lactis was included in combinations with fiber.
B. lactis.food_sources: Kefir, yogurt, fermented foods, but the B. lactis strain is not specified or guaranteed.
B. lactis.guidelines: MA 2022 (Clin Nutr): B. lactis with a significant effect on stool frequency in constipation. Cochrane 2023: on probiotics for functional abdominal pain - low certainty.
B. lactis.how_to_choose: It is B. lactis, and not mixtures: the effect has been confirmed for constipation in adults. Dietary fiber is a separate strategy and not a replacement for a probiotic.
mechs: Increase in the relative abundance of bifidobacteria in the intestines with fiber intake
Stimulation of intestinal motility and transit
Frequency of bowel movements due to chronic constipation (SMD 0.71)
Changing the composition of the microbiota and reducing inflammation
Improvement in symptoms of functional abdominal pain
B. lactis.myths: “Probiotics treat constipation” - the effect is shown only for B. lactis, mixtures and other strains make no difference. “Stool consistency improves” – no (SMD 0.26, p=0.08). “Data for diabetes - about a probiotic” - it’s about fiber.
B. lactis.name: B. lactis
B. lactis.onset: Within a week of treatment: stool frequency and symptoms improved throughout the course.
B. lactis.title: B. lactis
B. lactis.who_needs: Adults with chronic constipation - increased bowel movements (SMD 0.71). Children with functional abdominal pain - overall effect of probiotics (RR 1.57), low confidence.

B1.about: Thiamine (B1) is a nerve tissue vitamin: in peripheral neuropathy, including alcoholic, treatment with B1 improves symptoms; healthy people without data deficits have no data.
B1.caution: In normal doses, thiamine is safe; ESPEN points out the importance of correct status assessment; For alcoholic neuropathy, the key is to abstain from alcohol.
B1.course: Weeks-months, in parallel with eliminating the cause (abstinence from alcohol).
B1.food_sources: Whole grains, legumes, pork, nuts, yeast; with alcoholism and heat treatment, absorption decreases.
B1.guidelines: SR 2019: for alcoholic polyneuropathy - B-complex with thiamine. MA 2021: B1 improves symptoms (OR 5.34 [1.87-15.19]). ESPEN 2022: micronutrient status monitoring.
B1.how_to_choose: Benfotiamine or thiamine in B-complex; dose - according to confirmed deficiency; with alcoholism, prevention against deficiency, and not “just in case.”
mechs: Replenishment of B1 in case of deficiency: coenzyme of energy metabolism of nervous tissue
improvement in symptoms of peripheral neuropathy (OR 5.34)
B-complex with thiamine for alcoholic polyneuropathy
relief of sensory neuropathy in chronic alcohol users
Treatment with B-vitamins without regard to baseline status (common RCT pool)
trend towards improvement without statistical significance (OR 2.58)
B1.myths: “B1 pumps up a healthy brain” - in MA 2021, the effect is only in patients with neuropathy (n=3). “An alcoholic has enough vitamins” - neuropathy in alcoholism in 46%. “The more, the better” - they check the status, not megadoses.
B1.name: Vitamin B1
B1.onset: Course - weeks: for neuropathy, treatment with B1 significantly improved symptoms (MA 2021); There is no acute effect like stimulants.
B1.title: Vitamin B1
B1.who_needs: Chronic alcohol consumers (risk of neuropathy 46.3%); patients with peripheral neuropathy - improvement in symptoms (OR 5.34); with normal B1 status there is no evidence.

B12.about: Methionine synthase cofactor: critical in deficiency; does not improve cognition and energy in healthy people.
B12.caution: Oral B12 (1000-2000 mcg/day) is as effective as injections for maintaining levels (Cochrane). For cognitive functions in healthy people there is NO effect. Critical for vegans and the elderly with atrophic gastritis. For pernicious anemia - injections.
B12.food_sources: Meat, fish, eggs, dairy products; algae and yeast are unreliable sources, vegans need a supplement.
B12.guidelines: Oral = injections according to B12 level (NMA 2024, 4275); vegans have a higher functional deficit; STI - risk +42% (SR 2023).
B12.how_to_choose: 500–1000 mcg orally/sublingually; for deficiency or vegans; before taking - B12 + MMA + homocysteine.
mechs: Participation in the methionine/folate cycle and erythropoiesis: hemoglobin synthesis, homocysteine reduction
Hemoglobin and homocysteine are normalized in case of deficiency
Absorption in the ileum depends on gastric acidity and intrinsic factor (PPIs interfere)
The risk of deficiency is higher in those taking PPIs and in the elderly
B12.myths: “Raises everyone’s energy” - in healthy people, cognition and fatigue do not change (16 RCT). “Injection only”—oral 1000–2000 mcg is just as effective.
B12.name: Vitamin B12
B12.onset: If there is a deficiency, it takes weeks to restore the level; There is no immediate “rush of energy”.
B12.title: Vitamin B12
B12.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
B12.who_needs: Vegans, elderly (atrophic gastritis), taking PPIs, pregnant women with deficiency; pernicious anemia - injections only.

B2.about: Riboflavin (B2): 400 mg/day for 3 months significantly reduces the frequency, duration and pain of migraine (MA 2022); Vegans have a risk of deficiency.
B2.caution: Water soluble; There are no significant AEs reported in the abstracts at 400 mg/day.
B2.course: 3 months according to the MA 2022 scheme, then according to dynamics.
B2.food_sources: Milk, eggs, meat, liver, mushrooms, whole grains; with veganism, intake is often lower than normal (SR 2021).
B2.guidelines: MA 2022 (8 RCT + 1 clinical, n=673): 400 mg/day 3 months - frequency (p=.001), days (p=.005), duration (p=.003), pain (p=.015); SR 2021: Low B2 intake in vegans.
B2.how_to_choose: Regular riboflavin 400 mg for migraines; in B-complexes the dose is lower and the goal is different; Check the form and dosage on the label.
mechs: Energy metabolism coenzyme, participation in mitochondrial metabolism
migraine prevention 400 mg/day – reduction in 4 outcomes
Addressing the Risk of Low Intake When Vegan
prevention of B2 deficiency, but not cure
B2.myths: “B2 is just a vitamin for energy” - strong data specifically for migraines. “The vitamin has no effect on migraine” - MA from 9 studies (n=673) showed an improvement in all 4 outcomes. “Any dose works” - the effect is described for 400 mg/day.
B2.name: Vitamin B2
B2.onset: Prevention of migraine - a course of 3 months (MA 2022): significantly fewer days, duration, frequency and pain.
B2.title: Vitamin B2
B2.who_needs: Migraine sufferers - prevention 400 mg/day, 3 months; vegans and vegetarians - risk of low B2 intake; “for everyone’s energy” - no data.

B3.about: Nicotinamide (form B3): reduces the risk of non-melanoma skin cancer in people with a history of it (RR 0.50, MA 2022); the effect is not shown in healthy people.
B3.caution: Increased risk of GI AEs (MA 2022); niacin forms give flushing; if there is a history of skin cancer, a doctor’s prescription.
B3.course: Long-term, as long as prevention is relevant (according to RCT schemes in MA 2022).
B3.food_sources: Meat, poultry, fish, liver, peanuts; Cereal niacin is absorbed less well - nutrition is not detailed in the abstracts.
B3.guidelines: MA 2022 (29 trials, n=3039): Nicotinamide reduces skin cancer - RR 0.50 [0.29-0.85], moderate potency; weak recommendation for persons with a history of skin cancer.
B3.how_to_choose: Nicotinamide (not niacin - no flushing) in chemoprophylaxis doses under the supervision of a physician; topical forms - for hyperpigmentation.
mechs: Nicotinamide: NAD+ restoration and DNA repair
lightening of dark spots with high quality examinations
B3.myths: “The data on the reduction in LDL relate to niacin” - that MA is about statins and has nothing to do with B3. “More B3 is healthier” - nicotinamide has GI AEs. “Everyone needs B3 for their skin” - evidence for high-risk groups.
B3.name: Vitamin B3
B3.onset: Chemoprophylaxis - in a course while taking it; in MA the effect on skin cancer and actinic keratoses is significant, GI AEs are possible.
B3.title: Vitamin B3
B3.who_needs: People with a cancerous field or a history of skin cancer - chemoprophylaxis with nicotinamide (GRADE weak); for hyperpigmentation - topically; There is no data for “everyone’s” metabolism.

B5.about: Pantothenic acid (B5): the benefits of dietary supplements have not been confirmed in abstracts; deficiency - in spinal cord injuries; topical dexpanthenol is no better than others.
B5.caution: The safety of high doses is not reported in the abstracts; In case of SM injuries, the nutritional picture is complex.
B5.dosage: No data: B5 dietary supplement has not been studied in abstracts.
B5.food_sources: Widely distributed: meat, liver, eggs, legumes, whole grains; severe deficiency is rare.
B5.guidelines: CP 2019 (SCI): B5 Deficiency in Chronic Spinal Cord Injury—A Matter of Screening, Not Supplementation; SR 2005: topical dexpanthenol is no better than other treatments for nipple pain.
B5.how_to_choose: There is no data for choosing a form; if a deficiency is suspected, assess the status; in B-complexes it is harmless, no benefits beyond the norm have been shown.
mechs: no better than other products in the 2005 review
B5 deficiency in patients with chronic spinal cord injury
malnutrition indicator; the benefits of supplements have not been shown
B5.myths: “B5 is the vitamin of beauty and nerves” - there is no data in the abstracts. “Dexpanthenol treats pain during feeding” - in CP, no topical drug has surpassed the others. “Useful just in case” - without a deficiency the effect has not been proven.
B5.name: Vitamin B5
B5.onset: Not described: in abstracts, the use of B5 dietary supplements and the timing of the effect were not studied.
B5.title: Vitamin B5
B5.who_needs: Groups at risk for deficiency (chronic spinal cord injury - SR 2019), but there is no evidence of benefit from supplements; There are no indications for healthy people with a normal diet.

B6.about: Pyridoxine (B6): reduces nausea and vomiting during pregnancy (MA 2023); for neuropathy as monotherapy has not been studied, and high doses themselves are toxic to the nerves.
B6.caution: High doses → sensory axonal neuropathy, symptoms improve after discontinuation (CP 2023); during pregnancy, the dose is as per the doctor.
B6.course: For the period of symptoms of nausea/vomiting during pregnancy.
B6.food_sources: Chicken, fish, liver, potatoes, bananas, chickpeas, whole grains; During heat treatment, losses are significant.
B6.guidelines: MA 2023 (18 studies): pyridoxine alone and in combination - Rhode's 0.78 [0.26-1.31], PUQE 0.75 [0.28-1.22]; CP 2023: high doses of B6 - risk of neurotoxicity.
B6.how_to_choose: Pyridoxine in doses for NVP under the supervision of a physician; do not take megadoses; For neuropathy, do not prescribe alone.
mechs: High B6 Levels and Sensory Axonal Neuropathy
neurotoxicity in excess, improvement after withdrawal
B6 as part of a combination treatment for neuropathy
monotherapy has not been studied - the role has not been confirmed
B6.myths: “B6 heals nerves” - in CP 2023 there is no data on B6 as a monotherapy for neuropathy. “More B6 is better” is the opposite: high levels cause sensory axonal neuropathy. “Natural means safe” – the dose decides.
B6.name: Vitamin B6
B6.onset: For nausea during pregnancy - improvement during use (MA 2023); No deadlines have been established for other indications.
B6.title: Vitamin B6
B6.upper_limit: not established (not given in abstracts; high doses are neurotoxic)
B6.who_needs: Pregnant women with nausea/vomiting - pyridoxine alone or in combination; for neuropathy - only as part of dose-controlled treatment; high doses - risk of sensory neuropathy.

B9.about: Methyl cycle coenzyme: critical for the fetal neural tube, reduces homocysteine.
B9.caution: Folic acid (vitamin B9). 12 Cochrane reviews in the database! For the prevention of neural tube defects: Cochrane supports efficacy (400 mcg/day 1–3 months before conception and in the first trimester). For pregnancy: Cochrane. To reduce homocysteine: works. For cognitive function in older people: Cochrane shows no benefit. Caution: masks B12 deficiency in the elderly. Methylfolate (5-MTHF) is the active form for people with the MTHFR polymorphism.
B9.food_sources: Spinach, liver, legumes - but folate is labile and is less absorbed; synthetic is more reliable.
B9.guidelines: 400 mcg/day periconceptively (WHO); homocysteine ​​- dose according to analysis. There was no effect on preterm birth (Cochrane).
B9.how_to_choose: Regular folate 400–800 mcg; for MTHFR - 5-MTHF (methylfolate). In complexes, look for exactly these doses.

interactions.note: antagonist, reduces the effect of chemotherapy

mechs: Deficit Cognition/Mood; methylfolate adjunctive in depression
The methyl cycle in embryogenesis: closure of the neural tube
Folate sufficiency in pregnancy: hematology and homocysteine
Folate/hemoglobin is higher, homocysteine is lower; birth outcomes unchanged
B9.myths: “All B vitamins are the same” - it is periconceptive folate (RR 0.28) that closes the topic of the neural tube. “Memory for the elderly” - Cochrane showed no benefit.
B9.name: Vitamin B9
B9.onset: 1–3 months before conception; homocysteine ​​in weeks; for cognition in the elderly - no effect.
B9.title: Vitamin B9
B9.who_needs: Planning/pregnant women (neural tube), with elevated homocysteine, vegans, elderly with a deficiency according to analysis.

BCAA.about: Leucine/isoleucine/valine: there is no sports effect with enough protein; niche - hepatic encephalopathy.
BCAA.caution: BCAA (leucine/isoleucine/valine). For hepatic encephalopathy in cirrhosis: 4 Cochrane reviews show effectiveness. For sports: meta-analyses are inconsistent - many show no clinically significant effect. For sarcopenia in cirrhosis: data available. For oncology/surgical: limited data.
effects: There is no effect with enough protein (not confirmed)
BCAA.food_sources: Eggs, meat, milk, soy: All protein contains BCAA - it's easier to eat protein than a supplement.
BCAA.guidelines: Cochrane 2017: BCAA reduces symptoms of encephalopathy (16 RCT), does not change mortality; There is no benefit for sports.
BCAA.how_to_choose: Take the supplement only for cirrhosis with encephalopathy; It makes no sense for sports - protein/protein is more effective.
mechs: There is no effect with enough protein
Hepatic encephalopathy: fewer symptoms (Cochrane, 827 people); no for mortality
BCAA.myths: “They build muscles without food” - there is no effect if there is enough protein. “They treat the liver” - only for encephalopathy with cirrhosis, they do not affect mortality.
BCAA.name: BCAA
BCAA.onset: Encephalopathy: symptomatically, in courses; for muscles there is no immediate effect.
BCAA.title: BCAA
BCAA.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
BCAA.who_needs: Cirrhosis with hepatic encephalopathy; athletes/vegans with a lack of protein - but just protein is better.

CDP-холин.about: Choline donor for acetylcholine and membranes; effect on cognitive decline in patients, not in healthy people.
CDP-холин.caution: Citicoline (CDP-choline) is a precursor to phosphatidylcholine. For acute ischemic stroke: there is evidence, but recent reviews show limited effectiveness. For cognitive impairment and dementia: evidence is mixed. Safe in standard doses (1000-2000 mg/day). Used in Europe and Asia as a medicine.
CDP-холин.food_sources: Choline is found in eggs, liver, legumes; but citicoline is a pharmaceutical form and cannot be obtained from food.
CDP-холин.guidelines: Cochrane 2020 (stroke): no effect; MA 2023 (MCI/dementia): cognition better (SMD 0.56–1.57), quality low.
CDP-холин.how_to_choose: 250–500 mg of citicoline in courses for cognitive complaints in the elderly; healthy people without a diagnosis - do not take it.
mechs: Memory in the elderly/under stress, weak in healthy people
Resynthesis of membrane phospholipids during ischemia
Acute ischemic stroke: no effect on GRADE mortality/disability (10 RCT, 4281)
Cholinergic support for dementia and MCI
MCI/AD/post-stroke dementia: better cognition (SMD 0.56–1.57), poor RCT quality
CDP-холин.myths: “Saves in case of stroke” - does not change mortality/disability (10 RCT, 4281). “Nootropic for healthy people” – patients’ niche.
CDP-холин.name: CDP-Choline
CDP-холин.onset: Course effect: cognitive shifts over weeks and months; does not provide sharp “clarity”.
CDP-холин.title: CDP-Choline
CDP-холин.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
CDP-холин.who_needs: Elderly with mild cognitive decline and post-stroke dementia (as prescribed); healthy for the “brain” - there is no effect.

CoQ10.about: Mitochondria electron carrier and antioxidant; niche - heart failure (Cochrane).
CoQ10.caution: Coenzyme Q10 (ubiquinone/ubiquinol). For heart failure: 2 Cochrane reviews confirm effectiveness (reduction in mortality, hospitalization). For blood pressure: 2 Cochrane reviews show a decrease. For statin myopathy: data are conflicting. For migraine: limited data. Dose: 100-300 mg/day. Ubiquinol (active form) is more bioavailable, but more expensive.
CoQ10.food_sources: Meat, fish, and offal provide milligrams; You cannot get a dose of 100–200 mg from food.
CoQ10.guidelines: Cochrane 2021: Possible mortality and hospitalization benefits for HF; for hypertension the effect is unreliable.
CoQ10.how_to_choose: Ubiquinone 100–300 mg/day; ubiquinol is more bioavailable, but more expensive; with statins the level drops.
mechs: Energy in statin users/elderly; in healthy people it is weak
Antioxidant and stabilization of myocardial calcium-dependent channels
Ubiquinone deficiency correlates with severity of heart failure
Cochrane review: effect on BP in primary hypertension is uncertain
CoQ10.myths: “Energy for everyone” - no effect in healthy people, niche - heart failure. “Reduces blood pressure” - Cochrane considers the effect unreliable.
CoQ10.name: CoQ10
CoQ10.onset: Delayed, in courses: less mortality and hospitalization for HF; There is no instant charge.
CoQ10.title: CoQ10
CoQ10.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
CoQ10.who_needs: Heart failure as part of therapy; elderly and on statins; for hypertension and healthy people - there is little data.

D-манноза.about: Sugar that blocks E. coli adhesion: in case of recurrent UTIs, the data are contradictory, fresh LA is zero.
D-манноза.caution: D-mannose is a simple sugar. Popular for preventing urinary tract infections (especially recurrent UTIs). Mechanism: prevents the adhesion of E. coli to the epithelium of the bladder. Selected RCTs show comparable efficacy to antibiotic prophylaxis, but there are NO systematic reviews in PubMed. Dose: 1-2 g/day. Safe. High-quality meta-analyses are needed.
effects: Recurrent UTI: promising, MA is small
D-манноза.food_sources: D-mannose - simple sugar from berries and fruit juices; workers 1-2 g are more convenient from powder/tablets.
D-манноза.guidelines: Cochrane 2022: low evidence; MA 2025 (6 RCT, 1167): RR 0.57 NS; MA 2020: RR 0.23; RCT 2026 - antibiotics are stronger.
D-манноза.how_to_choose: 1-2 g/day course; adjuvant/prophylaxis only, not treatment for UTI; if you have symptoms, call a doctor.
mechs: Blocks FimH E. coli - no adhesion
Recurrent UTI: promising, MA is small
Antiadhesion of uropathogenic E. coli to the urothelium, elimination in urine
Recurrence of UTI: MA controversial (2020 RR 0.23, 2025 null)
Prevention of relapses in users without a catheter (anti-adhesion)
UTIs are less common, disease-free period is longer, QoL is higher (n=695, 2021)
D-манноза.myths: “An alternative to antibiotics” - MA 2025 did not find any effect (RR 0.57, NS). “Better than antibiotics” - RCT 2026: 0.2 vs 0.32 episodes.
D-манноза.name: D-Mannose
D-манноза.onset: Course, prophylactic: 1-2 g/day; There is no one-time “treatment” - antibiotics are faster.
D-манноза.title: D-Mannose
D-манноза.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
D-манноза.who_needs: Women with recurrent UTIs who need non-drug prevention; fresh MA does not show any effect.

DHA.about: DHA in Alzheimer's disease slows progression on the CDR scale (SMD -0.41), but MMSE and ADAS-cog make no difference; the effect is not shown in healthy people.
DHA.caution: GI side effects are the most common; the drug with EPA and DHA had a negative effect on ventricular volume. Does not replace primary therapy.
DHA.course: Long-term use as part of the treatment of Alzheimer's disease; for nursing mothers - for the entire period of breastfeeding.
DHA.dosage: Doses are not given in the abstracts: different combinations of EPA, DHA and medications with them were used.
DHA.food_sources: Fatty fish - salmon, mackerel, herring, caviar; The DHA content in milk depends on the mother's diet.
DHA.guidelines: MA 2024 in Alzheimer's: CDR slowing of progression (SMD -0.41), MMSE and ADAS-cog without significant differences. SR 2021: Omega-3 and -6 are less effective.
DHA.how_to_choose: For Alzheimer's - n-3-PUFA; studies have found no differences between individual supplements. For postpartum depression, the concentration of DHA in milk is important.
mechs: Incorporation into neuronal membranes and anti-inflammatory effect
Substrate for retinal and brain tissue membranes
Association of high concentrations of DHA in milk with the incidence of postpartum depression
DHA.myths: “Omega-3 protects everyone’s brain”—supplements are less effective for neurodegeneration. “Improves memory for healthy people” - not confirmed in abstracts. “The more, the better” - the most often noted GI side effects.
DHA.name: DHA
DHA.onset: For Alzheimer's - as part of long-term use; however, no significant changes were recorded in MMSE and ADAS-cog.
DHA.title: DHA
DHA.who_needs: Patients with confirmed Alzheimer's disease - according to the CDR scale. Nursing mothers: high concentrations of DHA in milk are considered protective factors. There is no data for healthy people.

EPA.about: EPA - omega-3 with anti-inflammatory effect: linearly reduces triglycerides and non-HDL (90 RCT) and alleviates depression with formulas with EPA ≥60% at a dose of ≤1 g/day.
EPA.caution: The safety of high doses has not been addressed in the abstract; against the background of anticoagulants and high doses (>2-4 g/day) - consult a doctor.
EPA.course: Course - weeks-months; The decrease in triglycerides lasts while taking it.
EPA.dosage: Depression: EPA ≤1 g/day (forms with EPA ≥60%); lipids: total dose of omega-3 >2 g/day.
EPA.food_sources: Products are not listed in the abstracts; the standard is oily fish and fish oil, but the evidence relates to supplementation with a specified dose of EPA.
EPA.guidelines: MA 2023 (90 RCT, 72,598): omega-3 linearly reduces TG and non-HDL, clearly at doses >2 g/day; MA 2019 (26, 2160): EPA ≥60% ≤1 g/day for depression (SMD −0.28).
EPA.how_to_choose: See mg EPA and EPA proportion ≥60%; for depression ≤1 g/day EPA; with lipids >2 g/day; Avoid DHA-dominant formulas for mental health purposes.
mechs: TG and non-HDL - linear at doses >2 g/day (90 RCT)
there is no significant improvement - the effect is associated with EPA
EPA.myths: “Any omega-3 is the same” - DHA-pure did not improve depression (MA 2019). “Reduces cholesterol” - no: triglycerides and non-HDL, LDL - J-shaped. “1 g per day for everyone” - for lipids you need more than 2 g/day.
EPA.name: EPA
EPA.onset: Lipids - dose-dependent, course (weeks) at doses >2 g/day; depression - weeks or months of use, the effect according to MA 2019 is not acute.
EPA.title: EPA
EPA.who_needs: Hypertriglyceridemia, especially in obesity - omega-3 >2 g/day; depression - formulas ≥60% EPA ≤1 g/day; the effect is specifically EPA: DHA-pure has not shown any benefit for mental purposes.

GLA.about: GLA (evening primrose oil): for atopic dermatitis in children there are indications of benefit in case of poor quality of work; Ineffective for acne and psoriasis.
GLA.caution: Ineffective for acne, psoriasis, chronic manual dermatitis, hepatitis B, preeclampsia and Sjögren's syndrome.
GLA.course: A course of weeks-months according to schemes from research; exact terms are not given in abstracts.
GLA.food_sources: Flax, hemp, and soy contain trace amounts of GLA; a practical source is evening primrose seed oil.
GLA.guidelines: EAACI 2024: Insufficient evidence for evening primrose. Review 2024: No strong recommendations for inflammatory conditions due to heterogeneity.
GLA.how_to_choose: For skin - Oenothera biennis oil; take into account the low quality of research. For arthritis and diabetes, there is insufficient data to make a choice.
mechs: Substrate for prostaglandins and anti-inflammatory mediators
Relief of symptoms of atopic dermatitis
Support barrier function and skin hydration
Improved skin condition in healthy volunteers
Metabolism of GLA into leukotrienes and anti-inflammatory mediators
GLA.myths: “Primrose heals the skin” - data relate to atopic dermatitis in children. “It will help with joints” - with rheumatoid arthritis, the results are mixed. “Proven” - quality according to Jadad is low, review 2024 requires caution.
GLA.name: GLA
GLA.onset: Within the framework of the reception, weeks-months; for dermatitis, the assessment is based on the SCORAD scale, the rate in abstracts is not specified.
GLA.title: GLA
GLA.who_needs: Children with atopic dermatitis without food allergies - there is evidence of improvement in symptoms. Ineffective for acne, psoriasis, PMS, dry eyes and preeclampsia.

HMB.about: HMB is a metabolite of leucine: preserves muscle in cancer patients (review 2022) and increases walking speed in sarcopenia with exercise (MA 2024).
HMB.caution: In reviews, safety was comparable to placebo; the effects are concentrated in clinical groups—do not exaggerate expectations in healthy people.
HMB.course: Weeks to months, along with a training program or nutritional support.
HMB.dosage: Ca-HMB 3 g/day (80% of studies in SR 2022).
HMB.food_sources: HMB - metabolite, no food source; substrate leucine - in meat, fish, eggs, dairy products.
HMB.guidelines: JCSM 2022 (CP 15 papers, cancer): muscle mass 4/4, function 2/2, hospitalizations 3/3; MA 2024 (5 RCT): walking speed SMD 0.48; umbrella 2021: low-moderate confidence.
HMB.how_to_choose: Ca-HMB form, ~3 g/day (according to research schemes); target groups - patients and elderly people with stress; There is no data for sports outside the context of these reviews.
mechs: Slows muscle protein breakdown and supports protein synthesis
preservation of muscle mass and function in patients with cancer (4/4)
HMB and clinical outcomes in risk groups
reduction in hospitalizations, trend towards better survival
HMB.myths: “HMB is an anabolic for everyone” - data mainly in patients and the elderly. “Works on its own” - effects are often combined. “Added and the muscles grow” - no effect was found on grip strength and weight in MA 2024.
HMB.name: HMB
HMB.onset: Course from weeks to months: effects on weight and function are described when taking ~3 g/day; in MA 2024, walking speed increased as part of training.
HMB.title: HMB
HMB.who_needs: Patients with cancer under therapy - maintenance of muscle mass (Ca-HMB ~3 g/day in 80% of studies); elderly with sarcopenia - as part of exercise programs; otherwise data is limited.

L-Теанин.about: Green tea amino acid: calm focus and less stress; 200 mg over 30-60 minutes improves attention.
L-Теанин.caution: L-theanine is an amino acid found in tea. A meta-analysis of 31 RCTs showed improved attention and reduced stress. Effect on sleep: Evidence is mixed. Synergy with caffeine is a classic nootropic stack. Safe in standard doses (100-200 mg/day). Does not cause drowsiness. Well tolerated.
L-Теанин.food_sources: Green tea: 5-20 mg per cup - far from effective; for 100-200 mg, concentrated forms are needed.
L-Теанин.guidelines: MA 2026 (31 RCT, 1168): attention SMD 0.51, stress 0.31, fatigue - none. SR 2026 (13, n=550): sleep 200-450 mg. No NYA.
L-Теанин.how_to_choose: Pure L-theanine 100-200 mg; with caffeine 2:1 for focus; without “sleep formulas”; as needed.
mechs: Modulation of glutamate, increase in EEG alpha rhythm
Stress reduction in stressful conditions (200-400 mg/day)
Relaxation without sedation: support onset and sleep quality
Falling asleep, maintaining sleep and feeling restored (200-450 mg/day)
L-Теанин.myths: “Theanine = tea” - 5-20 mg per cup, not 200. “Leds to sleep” - relaxation without sedation. “Treats anxiety” - modest, significant in 1 work.
L-Теанин.name: L-Theanine
L-Теанин.onset: Acutely: 200 mg over 30-60 minutes - better attention (SMD 0.51); sleep - course, 200-450 mg/day.
L-Теанин.title: L-Theanine
L-Теанин.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
L-Теанин.who_needs: Mental work under stress; “Jitter-free focus” (caffeine 2:1); sleep support 200-450 mg; anxiety - weak.

L-карнитин.about: Transports fatty acids to mitochondria; the effects are modest: ~1 kg of weight, small shift of markers in T2D.
L-карнитин.caution: Acetyl-L-carnitine for diabetic neuropathy: effect ONLY at a dose of >1500 mg/day, certainty VERY LOW. For moving lameness: the effect is insignificant. For weight loss/sports: NO systematic proofs. 2 of 4 studies were funded by the manufacturer.
effects: Weight: minimum (~1 kg); recovery is weak
L-карнитин.food_sources: Red meat is the main source; vegetarians/vegans are usually at the lower end of normal, but deficiency is rare.
L-карнитин.guidelines: ALC >1500 mg/d for neuropathy - certainty VERY LOW; T2D: per 1 g/day HbA1c −0.16% (Cochrane 2019/2024).
L-карнитин.how_to_choose: Regular L-carnitine for metabolism - 1–2 g/day; for neuropathy - acetyl-L-carnitine, doses according to the doctor.
mechs: Weight: minimum (~1 kg); recovery is weak
Neuroprotection and neurotrophy of peripheral nerves (acetyl-L-carnitine)
Diabetic polyneuropathy: adjunct, clinical benefit not proven
Metabolic support for muscles during ischemia (propionylcarnitine)
Dose-dependent improvement of cardiometabolic markers in T2D
T2D: per 1 g/day HbA1c −0.16%, BMI −0.37, LDL −0.11; the effect is small
L-карнитин.myths: “It will melt fat on mitochondria” - it is stated, but the effect is ~1 kg and is contradictory. “Vitamin therapy” is a dosage form (ALC/PLC), not a dietary supplement.
L-карнитин.name: L-Carnitine
L-карнитин.onset: Neuropathy - courses 6-12 months; T2D markers - 12-24 weeks; there is no immediate effect.
L-карнитин.title: L-Carnitine
L-карнитин.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
L-карнитин.who_needs: Diabetic neuropathy (>1500 mg/day ALC), T2D with metabolic targets, claudication; for healthy weight loss - weak.

L-цитруллин.about: Precursor of arginine and NO: increases arginine in plasma, gives a sports “pump”; does not reduce pressure.
L-цитруллин.caution: L-citrulline is a precursor of arginine and nitric oxide (NO). More effective than arginine itself (not metabolized into GI, raises arginine levels better). For blood pressure: meta-analyses show a modest reduction. For sports: improved performance and recovery. For erectile function: there is data. For preeclampsia: data available. Dose: 3-6 g/day. Safe.
L-цитруллин.food_sources: Watermelon water is a rich source; For a sports dose, a supplement is simpler (6–8 g malate).
L-цитруллин.guidelines: MA 2018: BP unchanged; SR 2025: arginine for preeclampsia RR 0.52 (LOW), citrulline - no data.
L-цитруллин.how_to_choose: Citrulline malate 6–8 g 60 minutes before exercise; more bioavailable than arginine, not metabolized in GI.
mechs: Increase in plasma arginine and nitrates/nitrites (NO substrate)
Direct vasodilation upon administration is inconsistent; ergogenic effect in terms of RCT
L-arginine precursor: a hypothetical NO pathway in pregnancy
Preeclampsia: no data for citrulline (1 RCT); arginine has RR 0.52
L-цитруллин.myths: “Reduces blood pressure” - MA 2018 without any effect on blood pressure. “Treats preeclampsia” - there is data for arginine (RR 0.52), citrulline - 1 RCT without effect.
L-цитруллин.name: L-Citrulline
L-цитруллин.onset: Acute effect when taken 60 minutes before exercise; there is no cumulative effect.
L-цитруллин.title: L-Citrulline
L-цитруллин.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
L-цитруллин.who_needs: Athletes under intense stress (citrulline malate 6–8 g); no benefit has been proven for preeclampsia.

LGG.about: Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG: ESPGHAN makes a strong recommendation for antibiotic prophylaxis of diarrhea; for gastroenteritis, it shortens the duration of diarrhea.
LGG.caution: The overall confidence in the data on probiotics in Cochrane 2020 is low; in severe and immunocompromised patients, use caution.
LGG.course: Course for the duration of taking antibiotics or until diarrhea disappears.
LGG.dosage: Abstracts indicate a daily dose of 10^10 CFU; smaller doses gave borderline results.
LGG.food_sources: Fermented dairy products - kefir, yogurt, but the GG strain in them is not guaranteed and is not specified.
LGG.guidelines: ESPGHAN 2016: Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG - moderate quality evidence, strong recommendation for antibiotic prophylaxis of diarrhea in children.
LGG.how_to_choose: Look specifically for Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG, indicating the strain and CFU number; other strains of L. rhamnosus are not considered equal.
mechs: Adhesion to intestinal epithelium and protection of mucosal barrier function
Reducing the duration of acute gastroenteritis in children
Reduction in the number of days of diarrhea (MD -0.85 days)
Regional variability of effect according to large studies
LGG.myths: “An all-purpose probiotic” - ESPGHAN recommends LGG only for the prevention of diarrhea due to antibiotics. “Treats C. difficile” - S. boulardii is recommended there. “One RCT does not make a difference” - a meta-analysis of 18 RCTs confirmed the effect.
LGG.name: LGG
LGG.onset: Within a dose, days: in a meta-analysis, the duration of diarrhea was reduced by an average of 0.85 days.
LGG.title: LGG
LGG.who_needs: Children on a course of antibiotics with risk factors - prevention of diarrhea; in acute gastroenteritis, it shortens its duration. Not recommended for adults.

MSM.about: Source of organic sulfur. Studied in RCT on osteoarthritis - effect comparable to NSAIDs in some studies, but with fewer side effects.
MSM.caution: Rarely - GI discomfort, headache, insomnia when taken in the evening. Safe for a long time. Not recommended during pregnancy - limited data.
MSM.course: 4-12 weeks for joints; 4-6 weeks for skin
MSM.food_sources: Trace amounts in milk, vegetables, grains, coffee. You can't get your dose from food.
MSM.guidelines: EFSA does not approve health claims, but MSM is widely used in veterinary medicine and sports nutrition.
MSM.how_to_choose: Pure MSM (optiMSM or equivalent) without DMSO contamination. Capsules or powder - there is no difference.

interactions.note: theoretically can enhance, but there is little data

mechs: Organic Sulfur Source: Supports Collagen and Keratin Synthesis
Inhibition of NF-κB and reduction of IL-6
MSM.myths: “Removes wrinkles” - no data. “Works in 3 days” - the effect is cumulative, the first changes after 2-4 weeks. “Improves everything at once” - only joints and inflammation.
MSM.name: MSM
MSM.onset: 2-4 weeks for joints; 4-6 weeks for skin.
MSM.title: MSM
MSM.upper_limit: There is no formal UL. Doses up to 6 g/day are well tolerated by most.
MSM.who_needs: People with osteoarthritis (knee pain). For chronic inflammatory conditions. In sports - for recovery.

NAC.about: Precursor of glutathione, the main cell antioxidant: fewer exacerbations of COPD, liver protection.
NAC.caution: N-acetylcysteine is a precursor of glutathione. 4 Cochrane reviews in the database! For COPD: reduces the frequency of exacerbations. For acute liver failure (non-paracetamol): Cochrane. For H. pylori (adjuvant): Cochrane. For sepsis: Cochrane. For psychiatry (OCD, trichotillomania, bipolar): there is RCT with positive data. Dose: 600-1200 mg 2 times/day. Safe, side effects: GI.
NAC.food_sources: There is no separate food source: NAC is a cysteine derivative; cysteine ​​is found in meat, eggs, and oatmeal.
NAC.guidelines: Cochrane: in COPD there are fewer exacerbations (RR 0.87) at doses up to 600 mg; there is no benefit for sepsis; for H. pylori - adjunct.
NAC.how_to_choose: Any L-form NAC, 600–1200 mg/day. Expensive “sports” versions are not needed - reviews are based on the classic form.

interactions.note: enhances the effect, risk of hypotension

mechs: Mucolytic and antioxidant effect: thinning mucus in the respiratory tract
Fewer exacerbations of COPD at 600 mg/day and below
Antimicrobial adjuvant: destruction of H. pylori biofilms, bactericidal activity
Higher eradication of H. pylori in combination with antibiotics
Glutathione precursor: neutralize toxic metabolites in the liver
Less risk of transplantation in paracetamol liver failure
NAC.myths: “Antioxidant = health” – did not reduce mortality in sepsis (Cochrane). “Higher dose is better” - for COPD >600 mg without benefit; works up to 600 mg.
NAC.name: NAC
NAC.onset: There is no immediate effect: with COPD, exacerbations are less frequent over a distance, NAC is taken in courses.
NAC.title: NAC
NAC.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
NAC.who_needs: For COPD with frequent exacerbations; liver failure (including paracetamol); resistant H. pylori.

NMN.about: The precursor of NAD+ is the “molecule of youth”; does not improve metabolism, strength and muscles in humans.
NMN.caution: NMN (nicotinamide mononucleotide) is a precursor to NAD+. For safety: data available (42514320) - good tolerability. For glucose and lipid metabolism: mixed data (39531138). For muscle mass: limited data (40275690). Most of the data are short-term RCTs. Long-term effects have not been studied. NOT proven to be effective for 'anti-aging' in humans.
NMN.food_sources: NMN in food is not practical: trace amounts (broccoli, avocado); supplements are the only way to work.
NMN.guidelines: SR 2026 (15 RCT, GRADE): Courses are transferable; no broad metabolic benefits; “rejuvenation” has not been confirmed.
NMN.how_to_choose: If tried: 250–1000 mg/d (RCT doses) in short courses; no metabolic effect should be expected.
mechs: Short courses are tolerable: AEs and ALT/AST unchanged
Safe 250–2000 mg/d, 14 days–24 weeks (15 RCT, GRADE)
No benefit on glucose/lipids/strength; DBP and HOMA-IR are only signals (MA)
NMN.myths: “Molecule of Youth” - glucose/lipids/muscles do not improve in humans (MA 2024-2025). “Expensive means it works” - there is no dose-dependent effect.
NMN.name: NMN
NMN.onset: From 14 days to 24 weeks (250–2000 mg/d), metabolism did not change; There is no “rejuvenation”.
NMN.title: NMN
NMN.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
NMN.who_needs: Not determined: no benefit for glucose/lipids/muscle in healthy people; weak signals - only in the elderly and with early metabolites. risks.

PABA.about: PABA as a supplement has not been confirmed: the only oral RCT is PABA potassium salt 12 g/day for systemic scleroderma, there is no difference with placebo.
PABA.caution: In the RCT, 18 patients on the active substance and 6 on placebo withdrew due to adverse reactions: gastrointestinal intolerance and headache.
PABA.course: in RCT - 48 weeks of continuous use; there are no other schemes in the pool
PABA.food_sources: In pool abstracts, food sources are not discussed; In the literature, PABA is found as a marker of the completeness of 24-hour urine collection, and not as a nutrient.
PABA.guidelines: There are no PABA recommendations in the pool: one negative RCT for systemic scleroderma and topical sunscreen tests are available.
PABA.how_to_choose: There is nothing to buy: there is no confirmed dose or form for oral administration, and external agents are a separate issue.
mechs: PABA potassium salt was administered orally to RCT for systemic scleroderma at a dose of 12 g/day
No skin changes were detected compared to placebo
In topical trials, the PFA method did not distinguish the 7% dimethyl-PABA formula from placebo
Sun protection effect of external form
There is no direct data on the effect of taking PABA on the human body in the pool
The effect of the supplement has not been confirmed
PABA.myths: “PABA is included in sunscreens, which means it is useful internally” - external means and oral administration are two different things. “Helps skin diseases” - PABA potassium salt did not differ from placebo in RCT.
PABA.name: PABA
PABA.onset: RCT lasted 48 weeks without effect; no positive response times were recorded in the pool.
PABA.title: PABA
PABA.who_needs: For no one according to the pool. For the skin, only topical PABA derivatives have been studied, not oral administration.

PQQ.about: A young supplement with noisy marketing. There are single RCTs on cognition in the elderly (small samples), most of the data are from animal models.
PQQ.caution: There is little data on humans - most of the research is on animals. RCT single, small samples. Not recommended during pregnancy. Rarely - insomnia when taken in the evening.
PQQ.food_sources: Trace amounts in natto, parsley, green tea, kiwi. You can't get your dose from food.
PQQ.guidelines: EFSA does not approve. In Japan it has been sold as a dietary supplement since the 1970s, but without strict health claims.
PQQ.how_to_choose: Standardized PQQ (BioPQQ or equivalent). Avoid cheap powders without COA.
mechs: Mitochondrial dehydrogenase cofactor: respiratory chain support
Antioxidant: stable over a wide pH range, withstands thousands of oxidative cycles
PQQ.myths: “Reverses mitochondrial aging” is an exaggeration. “Improves memory instantly” - no, the effect is weak and cumulative. CoQ10 has much more evidence.
PQQ.name: PQQ
PQQ.onset: 4-8 weeks; does not give acute effects.
PQQ.title: PQQ
PQQ.upper_limit: There is no formal UL. Doses up to 40 mg/day are considered safe.
PQQ.who_needs: Older adults interested in mitochondrial support. In sports - as “energy for cells”. The evidence base is weaker than that of CoQ10.

S. boulardii.about: Yeast probiotic: effective and safe in 84% of cases in 27 RCTs (5029 patients); reduces the risk of diarrhea with antibiotics (RR 0.47).
S. boulardii.caution: Safety confirmed in 27 RCTs and 5029 patients; in critically ill patients with central venous catheters was not assessed in abstracts.
S. boulardii.course: Course for the duration of taking antibiotics; for the prevention of diarrhea in travelers - from the beginning of the trip.
S. boulardii.food_sources: Not a food product, but a yeast preparation; kefir and sauerkraut are not sources of S. boulardii.
S. boulardii.guidelines: ESPGHAN 2016: S. boulardii - moderate quality, strong recommendation for antibiotic prophylaxis of diarrhea in children. WJG 2010: Strongly recommended for adults.
S. boulardii.how_to_choose: Indicate the S. boulardii strain and CFU number; ESPGHAN is recommended for the prevention of diarrhea in children. Combinations with zinc were studied separately.
mechs: Yeast probiotic competes with pathogens for adhesion to the intestinal epithelium
Reduced incidence of diarrhea with antibiotics (RR 0.47)
Production of antimicrobial metabolites and support of intestinal barrier function
Reducing the duration of acute diarrhea
Stabilization of microflora against the background of H. pylori eradication
Reduction of symptoms after H. pylori therapy
S. boulardii.myths: “Cures any diarrhea” is mainly prevention. “All probiotics are safe” – Cochrane 2020 has low quality of evidence. “It works the same for everyone” - with zinc the effect is stronger.
S. boulardii.name: S. boulardii
S. boulardii.onset: Prevention from the first day of antibiotics; for acute diarrhea, reduce the duration - within the limits of the dose, days.
S. boulardii.title: S. boulardii
S. boulardii.who_needs: Adults on a course of antibiotics - prevention of diarrhea; children - in combination with zinc for acute diarrhea. Treatment of diarrhea that has already begun—limited data.

SAMe.about: Methyl group donor; helps with depression (adjuvant), osteoarthritis pain and liver support.
SAMe.caution: SAMe (S-adenosylmethionine) is a universal donor of methyl groups. For depression: efficacy comparable to SSRIs in RCT. For osteoarthritis: A Cochrane review (19821403) confirms the analgesic effect. For the liver: there is data. For bipolar disorder: CAUTION (risk of mania). High price, low stability - enteric forms are needed. Dose: 400-1600 mg/day.
SAMe.food_sources: You cannot get it directly from food - it is synthesized by the body from methionine (eggs, fish, legumes).
SAMe.guidelines: Cochrane 2009: arthrosis pain −0.4 cm VAS, same function. Liver: 1000–1200 mg/d improves parameters (SR 2024).
SAMe.how_to_choose: Enteric forms, 400–800 mg/d on an empty stomach; for depression/bipolar - only with a doctor. Expensive.
mechs: Donor of methyl groups in the synthesis of NM
Pain: SMD −0.17, ~0.4 cm VAS; function without effect (4 RCT, 656)
Methylation in Hepatocytes: Support for Liver Diseases
Liver parameters are better, AEs are rare (1000–1200 mg/d; SR 15 articles)
SAMe.myths: “Instantly lifts the mood” - with major depression the effect is delayed. “Harmless in bipolar” - risk of mania, only with a doctor.
SAMe.name: SAMe
SAMe.onset: Depression: improvement in the first weeks; pain due to arthrosis - slight change by 1-3 months.
SAMe.title: SAMe
SAMe.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
SAMe.who_needs: Adults with depression (adjunct to therapy); for osteoarthritis - mild pain relief; with liver pathology.

Аланин.about: Meta-analysis in the pool - on β-alanine, which is a different substance than α-alanine; There is no data on α-alanine itself.
Аланин.caution: The pool mixes three topics: β-alanine for endurance, antidepressants and nutrition for female athletes; Alanine itself has not been studied.
Аланин.course: abstracts indicate only chronic use; specific duration not specified
Аланин.dosage: The meta-analysis noted that the total amount of β-alanine taken did not modify the effect; specific doses are not given in abstracts.
Аланин.food_sources: In the abstracts of the pool, food sources are not discussed: the meta-analysis on β-alanine concerned oral administration of the drug.
Аланин.guidelines: There are no recommendations for alanine in the pool: the only sports review is for female athletes, and there is no specific information about alanine there.
Аланин.how_to_choose: There is no data on α-alanine, there is nothing to buy. If you are interested in endurance, the pool only contains β-alanine.
mechs: In a meta-analysis of β-alanine, the effect on endurance performance at 0.5-10 minutes was 0.50 versus 0.11 for exercise performance.
Load duration significantly modified the effect (p = 0.004), but training and load mode did not
The effect depends on the type of load
A meta-analysis was performed for β-alanine; α-alanine was not used in pool work
The effect of α-alanine has not been studied
Аланин.myths: “Beta-alanine is alanine” - different substances: β-alanine goes into muscle carnosine, α-alanine has not been studied in any pool work. “There is data” - it is for β-alanine, the overall effect is 0.18 with 1461 participants.
Аланин.name: Alanine
Аланин.onset: The timing for α-alanine has not been studied; in the β-alanine meta-analysis, the protocols were chrotic only.
Аланин.title: Alanine
Аланин.who_needs: For anyone, according to the pool: There are no studies on α-alanine as a supplement. Data for β-alanine refer to a different substance.

Альфа-липоевая кислота.about: Antioxidant and coenzyme: sensory symptoms of diabetic polyneuropathy are lower; Doesn't help you lose weight.
Альфа-липоевая кислота.caution: Alpha lipoic acid (ALA) is an antioxidant. For diabetic peripheral neuropathy: A Cochrane review supports efficacy (600 mg/day IV or PO). For cardiometabolic factors: data available. For weight: the effect is small. For the liver (MASLD): data available. For fertility: limited data. Safe in doses of 300-600 mg/day. Caution: diabetes (reduce sugar, adjust insulin dose).
effects: Neuropathy: moderate; weight loss - no (not confirmed)
Альфа-липоевая кислота.food_sources: Liver, spinach, broccoli: ALA in bound form - the 600 mg studied cannot be obtained from food.
Альфа-липоевая кислота.guidelines: MA 2023 (10 RCT, 1242): sensory symptoms lower, dose-dependent; Cochrane 2024 (816) showed no benefit after 6 months.
Альфа-липоевая кислота.how_to_choose: 600 mg/day – research dose; higher only with a doctor; in case of diabetes, adjust glucose-lowering medications.
mechs: Reducing oxidative stress and improving nerve fiber microcirculation
Sensory symptoms of diabetic polyneuropathy are lower, dose-dependent (10 RCT, 1242 people)
Claimed disease-modifying effect in diabetic neuropathy
Cochrane review 2024: small/not significant effect on symptoms at 6 months (3 RCT, 816 people)
Альфа-липоевая кислота.myths: “Cures neuropathy” - Cochrane 2024 for 6 months there is almost no effect, improvement only in sensory symptoms (MA 2023). “Burns fat” - no effect.
Альфа-липоевая кислота.name: Alpha-Lipoic Acid
Альфа-липоевая кислота.onset: Effect over a distance of weeks (600–1800 mg/day); Cochrane 2024 sees no benefit for 6 months.
Альфа-липоевая кислота.title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid
Альфа-липоевая кислота.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
Альфа-липоевая кислота.who_needs: Diabetic polyneuropathy with sensory symptoms - under medical supervision, 600 mg/day; Don't rely on weight.

Аргинин.about: Nitric oxide precursor: weaker than citrulline for pumping; niches - preeclampsia, NEC in premature infants.
Аргинин.caution: L-arginine is a precursor of nitric oxide (NO). For the prevention of preeclampsia: there is data. For necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) in prematurity: Cochrane confirms effectiveness. For nitric oxide in angina: Cochrane. For blood pressure: moderate decrease. For erectile dysfunction: limited data (often with pycnogenol). For glycemic control: mixed evidence.
Аргинин.food_sources: Meat, poultry, fish, nuts, pumpkin seeds; but bioavailability from food is controversial - citrulline is easier.
Аргинин.guidelines: Preeclampsia: RR 0.52 (0.35–0.78, low confidence). NEC in prematurity: Cochrane. Sports: 3–6 g/day – consider GI.
Аргинин.how_to_choose: If arginine: L-form, without “technology”. Dose - according to the purpose of administration (preeclampsia / NEC - as prescribed by the doctor).
mechs: Precursor to NO, but bioavailability is low
NO substrate → vasodilation, prevention of preeclampsia
Preeclampsia: RR 0.52, severe 0.23 (2025, n=2028); confidence is low
NO substrate for GI endothelium in preterm infants
Аргинин.myths: “Powerful pumping” - low bioavailability, citrulline is better. “More is better” - above 6 g it hits the GI. “Treats preeclampsia” - only reduces the risk.
Аргинин.name: Arginine
Аргинин.onset: BP response over hours-days; preeclampsia - courses for weeks; in sports the effect is unpredictable.
Аргинин.title: Arginine
Аргинин.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
Аргинин.who_needs: Pregnant women at risk of preeclampsia, premature babies (NEC) - as prescribed by a doctor. L-citrulline is better for sports.

Астаксантин.about: Carotenoid: after exercise, creatine kinase is lower, skin is better; on VO2max and IVF outcomes - no.
Астаксантин.caution: Astaxanthin is a carotenoid from the algae Haematococcus pluvialis. For skin: a systematic review (32202443) shows improvement in parameters. For fertility: data available (39127677, 41714661). For sport/rehabilitation: limited data. For the liver: there is data. There is little data on clinical outcomes—mostly biomarkers. Safe at doses of 4-12 mg/day.
Астаксантин.food_sources: Originally a microalgae; in food (salmon, krill) the concentrations are low - working 3-6 mg from the supplement.
Астаксантин.guidelines: MA 2026 (24 RCT): creatine kinase SMD −0.45, LDH −0.93, VO2max without shift. Skin (SR 2021): 3-6 mg/day for texture/wrinkles.
Астаксантин.how_to_choose: 3-6 mg/day for skin, 4-12 mg/day with fats for recovery; standardization according to Haematococcus pluvialis.
mechs: Oocyte maturation is higher (MD 8.40); IVF/pregnancy outcomes do not change
Reduced markers of muscle damage after exercise
Creatine kinase is lower after training (SMD −0.45); performance does not increase
Photoprotection and regeneration of the epidermis
Wrinkles, skin texture, and skin moisture are better at 3–6 mg/day; little data
Астаксантин.myths: “Pumps up VO2max” - no (24 RCT), recovery works. “Cures infertility” - oocyte maturation is better, IVF without changes.
Астаксантин.name: Astaxanthin
Астаксантин.onset: Course course: skin - 3-6 mg/day for weeks; recovery markers - after exercise.
Астаксантин.title: Astaxanthin
Астаксантин.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
Астаксантин.who_needs: Recovery after training (muscle enzymes down); skin photoaging; fertility (oocyte maturation) - context.

Астрагал.about: Classic Chinese adaptogen. The main effect is immunomodulation, especially in immunocompromised patients.
Астрагал.caution: Caution for autoimmune diseases - stimulates the immune response. May enhance the effect of immunosuppressants/cyclosporine. During pregnancy, there is not enough data.
Астрагал.course: 4-12 weeks, courses; for immunity - during cold season
Астрагал.food_sources: It is not used as food - the root is taken as an extract, decoction or capsules.
Астрагал.guidelines: Not included in EFSA/FDA recommendations as a medicine. In China, it is officially approved as part of drugs. There are systematic reviews, but the quality of RCTs is average.
Астрагал.how_to_choose: Standardized extract for polysaccharides 10-20% or astrosides IV 0.5%. Avoid products without specified concentration.

interactions.note: may reduce the effect - stimulates the immune response
there is evidence of increased lithium levels in the blood

mechs: Polysaccharides (astragalans): activation of macrophages and NK cells
Saponins (astrosides): modulation of T cell response
Астрагал.myths: “Cures all diseases from aging to cancer” - no, only immunomodulation. “Works for everyone” - the effect is noticeable in people with initial fatigue, not in healthy people.
Астрагал.name: Astragalus
Астрагал.onset: 2-4 weeks for immune effect; does not work “here and now”.
Астрагал.title: Astragalus
Астрагал.upper_limit: There is no formal UL. Doses up to 3 g/day are well tolerated. IV forms - only in the clinic, not for independent use.
Астрагал.who_needs: Frequently ill people (there is RCT on ARI prevention). Patients with chronic fatigue. In complex therapy after infections.

Ашваганда.about: Adaptogen: reduces cortisol, anxiety, improves sleep.
Ашваганда.caution: Withania somnifera is an adaptogen. Meta-analyses show that the reduction in cortisol is significant, but the subjective perception of stress may not improve. Effective for sleep. Safety: good in short-term RCTs (4-12 weeks). Long-term data are limited. Caution: autoimmune diseases, pregnancy (teratogenicity in the preclinic).
Ашваганда.guidelines: EFSA: claims not approved; MA series - moderate effect on anxiety and sleep.
Ашваганда.how_to_choose: Standardization 5% withanolides (KSM-66, Sensoril); root, not leaves.
mechs: Reduced HPA axis hyperactivation in the evening: sleep-promoting effect of the extract
Better sleep quality, especially with insomnia (≥600 mg/day, ≥8 weeks)
Effect on glucose and lipid metabolism (experimental and early clinical data)
Glucose, HbA1c and lipids in diabetes mellitus
Ашваганда.myths: “Works immediately like a tranquilizer” - the effect is cumulative. “Any extract is the same” - withanolides decide.
Ашваганда.name: Ashwagandha
Ашваганда.onset: Anxiety and sleep - 4-8 weeks; cortisol - 2-4 weeks.
Ашваганда.title: Ashwagandha
Ашваганда.who_needs: Chronic stress, anxiety, insomnia (≥600 mg ≥8 weeks).

Бакопа.about: Nootropic: improves memory and learning (brain adaptogen).
Бакопа.caution: Bacopa monnieri is an adaptogen from Ayurveda. Meta-analysis 24252493 showed significant improvement in memory after 8-12 weeks. The effects are NOT felt immediately (unlike caffeine). Optimal dose: 300 mg/day standardized extract (50% bacosides). Safe in short-term RCT (4-12 weeks). Side effects: gastrointestinal (nausea, cramps).
Бакопа.food_sources: Not consumed as food (grass in supplements).
Бакопа.guidelines: EFSA: claims not approved; MA—moderate effect on memory.
Бакопа.how_to_choose: Standardization of 50% bacosides; with food (fat soluble).
mechs: Dose dependence: ≥600 mg/d bacosides - working memory up
Working memory: SMD ~2.0, better than ginkgo and low doses (29 RCT, 2107)
Speed of attention and response selection (cholinergic activation)
Trail B −17.9 ms, CRT −10.6 ms; 12 weeks (9 RCT, 518)
Бакопа.myths: “Works like piracetam” - the mechanism is different, slower. “Instant effect” - 8-12 weeks minimum.
Бакопа.name: Bacopa
Бакопа.title: Bacopa
Бакопа.upper_limit: 300-450 mg extract/day; higher - GI discomfort, fatigue.
Бакопа.who_needs: Age-related memory decline, students in session; healthy adults - working memory.

Берберин.about: Alkaloid: reduces sugar, improves insulin sensitivity.
Берберин.caution: Berberine is an alkaloid from plants. For glycemic control: Meta-analyses show comparable efficacy to metformin in some RCTs. For lipids: moderate reduction. For obesity and liver disease (NAFLD): data available. Dose: 500 mg 2-3 times a day. Side effects: gastrointestinal. Caution: CYP3A4 inhibitor - interacts with medications.
Берберин.dosage: 500 mg 2-3 times a day before meals
Берберин.guidelines: EFSA: claims not approved; series of MA - the effect is comparable to metformin.
Берберин.how_to_choose: Berberine HCl or phytosome; 500 mg 3 times/day with food.
mechs: AMPK activation: lipid profile and blood pressure
TG −23.7, TC −20.6, LDL −9.6, SBP −5.5, HDL +1.4 mg/dl (dose-response MA)
Берберин.myths: “Replace metformin” - the effect is similar, but there is less data. “Safe with statins” - interaction.
Берберин.name: Berberine
Берберин.title: Berberine
Берберин.who_needs: Prediabetes, metabolic syndrome, type 2 diabetes (moderate data).

Бета-аланин.about: Builds carnosine - a proton buffer in the muscle: support for work for 1-4 minutes; There is no effect on strength and VO2max.
Бета-аланин.caution: Effect ONLY on activity 1-4 minutes (anaerobic threshold). Increases carnosine in muscles. Side effect: paresthesia (skin tingling) - can be solved by splitting the dose (≤1.6 g per dose). Optimum: 4-6 g/day, 4-6 weeks.
Бета-аланин.food_sources: Meat and poultry contain carnosine and beta-alanine; doses of 3–6 g/day cannot be replaced with food.
Бета-аланин.guidelines: SR 2017: productivity has not increased, effort is lower; MA 2026 in women: TTE is higher (SMD 0.49), confidence is very low.
Бета-аланин.how_to_choose: Regular powder 3.2–6.4 g/day in fractions (≤1.6 g per dose - less tingling); "matrices" are not needed.
mechs: Accumulation of carnosine → buffering of H+ in muscle
H+ Buffering via Carnosine: Endurance in Women
Time to exhaustion is higher (SMD 0.49, 8 RCT); confidence is very low)
Modulation of fatigue perception and metabolic markers
Perceived effort is lower, fatigue markers are better; performance remains unchanged
Бета-аланин.myths: “Pumps everything up” - improvement in work 1–4 minutes; overall productivity (SR 2017) has not increased. “No fatigue” - only perceived effort is lower.
Бета-аланин.name: Beta-Alanine
Бета-аланин.onset: Accumulation of carnosine - 4+ weeks of intake; There is no immediate ergogenic effect.
Бета-аланин.title: Beta-Alanine
Бета-аланин.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
Бета-аланин.who_needs: Athletes in the anaerobic threshold zone (1–4 min): 4–6 g/day 4–6 weeks; strength and marathon runners - there is little data.

Бета-глюканы овса.about: Oat Soluble Fiber: Lowers LDL and cholesterol when high; FDA/EFSA approved.
Бета-глюканы овса.caution: Oat beta-glucans are soluble fiber. FDA health claim (USA) officially approved: 'soluble fiber from oats may reduce the risk of CVD by lowering cholesterol'. A meta-analysis (35631184) confirms a decrease in LDL in hypercholesterolemic individuals. The effect is dose dependent: optimum 3+ g/day. For glycemic control: data available. Safe.
Бета-глюканы овса.food_sources: Oatmeal, bran, whole oats: beta-glucan is concentrated in them; for 3 g/day - a serving of oatmeal.
Бета-глюканы овса.guidelines: The FDA and EFSA have approved the claim: 3 g/day reduces cholesterol. MA 2022 (13 RCT, 927): TC −0.24, LDL −0.27 mmol/l.
Бета-глюканы овса.how_to_choose: Oat beta-glucan 3 g/day - from oatmeal/bran or supplement; no claims about “detox”.
mechs: Binding of bile acids in the lumen: cholesterol down
No effect on TG and HDL (mechanism limited by cholesterol)
TG −0.04 and HDL 0.00 mmol/l: no effect (NS)
Бета-глюканы овса.myths: “Reduces TG and increases HDL” - has no effect on either one (MA 2022). “Beta-glucan is stronger than statins” - the reduction in LDL is modest.
Бета-глюканы овса.name: Oat Beta-Glucans
Бета-глюканы овса.onset: The effect is dose-dependent: at 3 g/day, LDL decreases over weeks of administration, not at once.
Бета-глюканы овса.title: Oat Beta-Glucans
Бета-глюканы овса.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
Бета-глюканы овса.who_needs: Hypercholesterolemia and high risk of CVD - lowering LDL as a dietary measure; in healthy people the effect is small.

Бетаин.about: Betaine moderately increases maximum strength, primarily in the legs, but at 4 g/day and longer it raises total cholesterol.
Бетаин.caution: At 4 g/day and longer, total cholesterol increases by 0.34 mmol/l; Data on efficacy and safety in the elderly are still insufficient.
Бетаин.course: From 7 days for power effects; in lipid metabolism studies - from 6 to 24 weeks.
Бетаин.food_sources: Food sources are not listed in the abstract: the studies used a betaine drug, not a dietary change.
Бетаин.guidelines: There are no clinical recommendations for betaine in the pool: three sources are reviews on aging, athletic performance and lipid metabolism.
Бетаин.how_to_choose: You should expect an effect only from regular use for at least 7 days; at doses above 4 g/day, it is necessary to take into account the increase in total cholesterol.
mechs: Betaine as a donor of methyl groups increases the concentration of S-adenosylmethionine
Betaine improves mitochondrial function, reduces oxidative stress and inflammation
In MA 17 studies, taking from 7 days gave an effect on maximum strength, stronger for the lower body
In MA 6 RCT at 4 g/day, total cholesterol increased by 0.34 mmol/l, LDL, HDL and triglycerides did not change
Increase in total cholesterol with long-term use
Бетаин.myths: “Works for any performance” - upper body, endurance and power in MA unchanged. “Reduces cholesterol” - on the contrary, the total increased by 0.34 mmol/l. “Protects the heart” - no connection with cardiovascular disease and diabetes has been identified.
Бетаин.name: Betaine
Бетаин.onset: A positive effect in strength appears when taken for 7 days - this is the minimum included in the meta-analysis.
Бетаин.title: Betaine
Бетаин.who_needs: Athletes who need maximum strength in the squat and bench press; For homocysteine, the data were reviewed and no association with heart disease or diabetes was found.

Биотин.about: Vitamin B7: useful only in cases of deficiency; in healthy people it has not been proven for hair/nails; distorts analyses.
Биотин.caution: Biotin (vitamin B7, vitamin H). There are NO systematic reviews or meta-analyses on clinical effects in healthy people. Biotin deficiency is rare (only with genetic diseases, long-term parenteral nutrition, consumption of raw egg whites). In healthy people with normal levels - supplements have no proven effect on hair/nails/skin. Side effects: distortion of laboratory tests (troponin, thyroid hormones).
effects: Hair/nails only in case of deficiency; interferes with analyzes
Биотин.food_sources: Eggs, liver, nuts, legumes, milk; Deficiency is unlikely with a normal diet.
Биотин.guidelines: MA 2022 (5 RCT, 445): TC −0.22 significant, glucose/TG on the borderline, insulin without effect. Risk: Immunoassay bias.
Биотин.how_to_choose: 30-100 mcg/day with food; 48 hours before thyroid/troponin tests, cancel; on hair - only in case of deficiency.

interactions.note: distorts the results, stop in 3 days

mechs: Hair/nails only in case of deficiency; interferes with analyzes
Coenzyme of four carboxylases: fatty acid metabolism/gluconeogenesis
In malnutrition and pregnant women, deficiency markers are lower; Glycemic control in T2D is questionable
Claimed glucose and lipid control in T2D
Total cholesterol is lower (−0.22); glucose/TG borderline significant; insulin without effect (5 RCT, 445)
Биотин.myths: “For hair and nails for everyone” - only in case of shortage. “Harmless in any dose” - distorts immunoassays (thyroid, troponin).
Биотин.name: Biotin
Биотин.onset: In case of shortage - for weeks; healthy people have no effect at all.
Биотин.title: Biotin
Биотин.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
Биотин.who_needs: Only confirmed deficiency (genetics, parenteral nutrition, raw eggs); healthy for hair/nails - not proven.

Бор.about: Boron in the pool is almost unstudied: two sources are about scaffolds for bone outside of humans and the third place in the network MA for drugs after lithotripsy.
Бор.caution: In the network MA, all drugs showed an acceptable safety profile, but there are no separate data on doses and risks of boron in the pool.
Бор.food_sources: In the pool abstracts, sources of boron are not discussed: both sources are about materials for bone and about drug therapy.
Бор.guidelines: There are no separate clinical recommendations for boron in the pool: two sources are a review of materials for bone tissue and a network MA for drugs.
Бор.how_to_choose: There is no data to guide the choice of form and dose: neither of the two sources evaluates boron supplementation.
mechs: Boron is included in the structure of hydroxyapatite scaffolds to enhance bone regeneration
The effect has been studied in vitro and in animal models
In the network MA for therapy after lithotripsy, boron supplementation took third place according to SUCRA (67.9%)
Third place among drugs after lithotripsy
There is no data on the effect of boron on people outside of these two works in the pool
The effect of the supplement has not been confirmed
Бор.myths: “Boron strengthens bones” - a source about scaffolds with boron in vitro and in animals, not about tablets. “Helps against stones” - only third in the network MA, SUCRA 67.9%, after tamsulosin with tadalafil.
Бор.name: Boron
Бор.onset: Not studied: there are no direct RCTs with boron in the pool.
Бор.title: Boron
Бор.who_needs: There is no data on the target group: neither of the two sources tested boron supplementation as a stand-alone treatment method.

Босвеллия.about: Indian Frankincense: Acids inhibit 5-LOX; pain and stiffness are lower with osteoarthritis.
Босвеллия.caution: Boswellia serrata - 'Indian incense'. For osteoarthritis: Aflapin standardized extract (38365549) shows improvement in pain/function. For inflammation: Inhibits 5-lipoxygenase (5-LOX), an alternative to NSAIDs. For asthma/IBD: limited data. There is little data (2 abstracts in the database). A standardized extract with ≥30% boswellic acids is required. Dose: 100-250 mg 2-3 times/day.
effects: Osteoarthritis pain: moderate, in MA comparable to NSAIDs
Босвеллия.food_sources: Non-food: Boswellia serrata (frankincense) resin; It is used as a supplement and cannot be obtained from food.
Босвеллия.guidelines: MA 2024 (9 RCT, 712): VAS and WOMAC pain −10.7, stiffness −5.5; Aflapin is stronger (−16.1 vs −4.7); AEs as placebo.
Босвеллия.how_to_choose: Extract with AKBA ≥30%, better standardized forms; 300-500 mg 2-3 times a day in a course.
mechs: Osteoarthritis pain: moderate, in MA comparable to NSAIDs
OA: VAS -10.7, WOMAC-pain and function -10.7 (9 RCT, 712 people)
Standardized forms are better than non-standardized ones
Aflapin is stronger than other extracts (VAS -16.1 vs -4.7); modified forms are the best WOMAC
Босвеллия.myths: “Treats asthma and IBD” - limited data, niche - joints. "All forms are the same" - Aflapin and modified forms are noticeably stronger.
Босвеллия.name: Boswellia
Босвеллия.onset: Symptomatic: Pain and function improve after weeks of taking the standardized extract.
Босвеллия.title: Boswellia
Босвеллия.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
Босвеллия.who_needs: Joint osteoarthritis (pain, stiffness, function) as an alternative/addition to NSAIDs; according to AEs it is safe in NMA.

Боярышник.about: Leaf/flower extract: in chronic heart failure, improves workload and symptoms, as an adjunct to therapy.
Боярышник.caution: Hawthorn (Crataegus spp.). For CHF: A Cochrane review (18254076) confirms improvement in symptoms (shortness of breath, fatigue) and exercise capacity. Used in European herbal medicine as an adjuvant. The effect develops after 4-8 weeks. Does not replace standard therapy for CHF. Safe in standard doses. Caution: digoxin (increases the effect), antihypertensive drugs.
Боярышник.food_sources: The berries are edible, but the working doses are a standardized extract of the leaves and flowers; You can’t pick up berries.
Боярышник.guidelines: Cochrane 2008 (14 RCT): load +5.35 W, higher tolerance; symptoms below; AEs are rare; only adjunct for heart failure.
Боярышник.how_to_choose: Standardized extract 600–1200 mg/day; only for heart failure as prescribed by a doctor and with checking for interactions.
mechs: Adjunct chronic heart failure: workload and tolerance
CH NYHA I-III: maximum load +5.4-7 W, higher tolerance (855/632 people)
Reduction in double product (HR x BP) and symptoms
With HF: shortness of breath and fatigue are lower; double product minus (-20)
Боярышник.myths: “Heals the whole heart” is only an adjunct for heart failure, not a replacement for therapy. “Safe with tablets” - risk with digoxin and antihypertensives.
Боярышник.name: Hawthorn
Боярышник.onset: Effect on endurance and symptoms - after 4-8 weeks of use; not visible in short courses.
Боярышник.title: Hawthorn
Боярышник.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
Боярышник.who_needs: CHF I–III NYHA - adjunct to standard therapy under a doctor; healthy and without a diagnosis there is no benefit.

Бузина.about: Elderberry for colds/flu: symptoms are shorter (MA 2019), but confidence is low; there is no prevention.
Бузина.caution: Sambucus nigra (black elderberry). Meta-analysis of RCT shows a significant reduction in the duration of ARI symptoms (~4 days). Effective against influenza A/B and rhinovirus infections. Safe in the short term. Caution: raw berries/leaves are toxic (cyanogenic glycosides) - standardized extracts only. There is little data (only 2 RCTs in the database).
Бузина.food_sources: Ripe berries - jam/syrups; raw and unripe are toxic; in the clinic - a standardized extract.
Бузина.guidelines: MA 2019 (n=180): symptoms are shorter. SR 2021 (5 RCT, GRADE): duration/severity; vs oseltamivir - fewer complications.
Бузина.how_to_choose: Standardized extract/syrup; on the first day of symptoms 5-7 days; not raw berries.
mechs: Anthocyanins: blockade of viral attachment + immunomodulation
Reduces the duration of colds/flu by 1-2 days; prevention - weak
Reducing the duration and severity of ARI/influenza (treatment)
Duration of flu/symptoms is lower; confidence is unstable (5 RCT, SR)
Lower risk of flu complications and AEs vs oseltamivir (SR 2021)
Бузина.myths: “Elderberry cures colds” - only shorter/easier, the risk does not decrease. “Works for everyone” - no. “Raw berries are good for you” - toxic, extracts.
Бузина.name: Elderberry
Бузина.onset: Course 5-7 days from the start of symptoms; effect - shorter/lighter; prevention - no.
Бузина.title: Elderberry
Бузина.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
Бузина.who_needs: Start of ARI/flu symptoms - shorten duration; when refusing oseltamivir, complications are rare; prevention - no.

Валериана.about: Valerian root: subjectively the quality of sleep is slightly better, objectively (time to fall asleep) - no effect.
Валериана.caution: Valerian officinalis (Valeriana officinalis). For insomnia: Meta-analyses are inconsistent, with some showing minimal improvement in falling asleep and others showing no effect. Review 17517355 is literally called 'safe but not effective'. For anxiety: A Cochrane review (17054208) shows limited evidence. The effect develops after 2-4 weeks (not instantaneous). Safe, non-addictive (unlike benzodiazepines). Dose: 300-600 mg extract.
Валериана.food_sources: Not a food: it is the root of the plant, used as an extract/powder; There are no working doses in food.
Валериана.guidelines: 2024 umbrella (insomnia): subjective sleep better, objective metrics without shift; 2023 umbrella: the effect is modest, the data quality is low.
Валериана.how_to_choose: 300-600 mg of extract before bedtime for a course of 2-4 weeks; do not exceed the dose, do not combine with sedatives without a doctor.
mechs: Anxiety disorders: the evidence base is minimal (1 RCT)
Subjective effect on sleep without objective metrics
Sleep: subjectively better (RR 1.37), latency unchanged (MA 18 RCT)
Валериана.myths: “Valerian = sleeping pill” - latency without shift (18 RCT). “Treats anxiety” - 1 RCT (n=36). “Doesn’t work” – subjectively better, RR 1.37.
Валериана.name: Valerian
Валериана.onset: There is no objective reduction in latency; subjective improvement is partial, course 2-4 weeks.
Валериана.title: Valerian
Валериана.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
Валериана.who_needs: Mild sleep complaints, where a placebo profile is sufficient; for severe insomnia and anxiety, there is little data.

Витамин A.about: Vitamin A is fat soluble and is needed for vision, skin and immunity; data on dietary supplements are mainly about correction of deficiency, and not about “improvement” in healthy people.
Витамин A.caution: Fat soluble - accumulates, ESPEN warns of potential toxicity; without monitoring status, high doses are not justified.
Витамин A.course: Course on Confirmed Deficiency with Reassessment of Status (ESPEN 2022).
Витамин A.food_sources: Liver, eggs, dairy products, yellow-orange vegetables (beta-carotene); absorption depends on fats in the diet.
Витамин A.guidelines: ESPEN 2022: status monitoring and toxicity accounting; SR 2024 (AGA): deficiencies - factors of alopecia, A not key; SR 2023: Food insecurity linked to shortages.
Витамин A.how_to_choose: Only with a confirmed deficiency and according to the doctor’s dosage; retinol and beta-carotene differ in toxicity; healthy people without a deficiency - not needed.
mechs: Replenishing A deficiency: retinol for vision, skin, immunity
correction of an established deficit - a basic need
for A, the data in the review is weak, emphasis is placed on B/D/Fe/Zn
deficiency is associated in 89% of studies, incl. by A
Витамин A.myths: “More A means better skin and hair” - in the AGA review, the emphasis is on B, D, Fe, Zn, the role of A is weak. “There are always enough vitamins” - when food supply is unsafe, deficiency is common. “A is harmless” - fat soluble, ESPEN is mindful of toxicity.
Витамин A.name: Vitamin A
